Subject: Model fit & evals - benchmark links and next steps

Hi Sarah,

Thanks again for the call this morning — really appreciated the context on Acme's agent summarization pipeline and the latency/throughput targets (p95 < 400ms for short replies, sustained throughput ~120 TPS during peak batching windows). I wanted to follow up with the model-fit recommendations and the benchmark artifacts I mentioned.

Quick recap / recommended starting models
- rw-7b-v2 (4-bit quant) — lowest-cost option, good for high-TPS inference; measured at ~220 TPS (batch=8) with p50 =~ 60ms, p95 =~ 320ms on A100-like nodes.
- rw-13b-v1 (mixed-precision) — balanced quality/latency; ~130 TPS (batch=8), p50 =~ 90ms, p95 =~ 380ms.
- rw-70b-v1 (FP16) — highest quality for complex summarization; ~18 TPS, p50 =~ 240ms, p95 =~ 520ms.

All numbers above are from the Redwood-verified performance profiles (link below) using your target prompt lengths (~120 tokens input, ~80 tokens output) and our continuous-batching runtime. These profiles include steady-state TPS and latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99).

Artifacts attached / links
- Attached: acme_eval_prompts.csv — the prompt set we used for the quick benchmark.
- Attached: redwood_perf_profiles.pdf — condensed performance profiles and config notes.
- Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/benchmarks/ACME-1792 (raw run logs + latency histograms)
- Profile: https://docs.redwood.ai/perf-profiles/rw-13b-v1 (sample Redwood-verified model profile)

Notes on configuration we used
- Batching: experiments used batch size 8 with dynamic batching enabled (this is the default for message-based workloads).
- KV/prefix caching: disabled for these synthetic runs; we can re-run with warm cache to show lower p50s for repeated prompts.
- Quantization: rw-7b-v2 numbers are for Q4_0 4-bit; rw-13b-v1 used mixed-precision kernels.

Next steps I recommend
1) Quick pilot: we can run an Acme-specific eval using your sample corpus (we'll use the attached prompt set as a starting point).
2) Regression checks: define a small set (50-100) of canary prompts you'd consider critical — we will run nightly evals and send quality/regression alerts.
3) Pilot kickoff: 2-week pilot with a dedicated test pool — we can set expected SLOs and a rollback policy.

If that sounds good, I can loop in Marissa (solutions) and Vanessa (onboarding) to set up the pilot and get you access to the dashboard. Proposed availability for a 30-min pilot kickoff: Thu 3/26 10:00-11:30 PT or Fri 3/27 09:00-11:00 PT.

Hi Sarah — great questions, answers below.

1) Caching: the rw-13b-v1 numbers I shared were without KV/prefix caching (cold cache). With a warm prefix cache we typically see p50 reduce by ~15-25% and p95 reduce by ~10-20% depending on prompt overlap. We can re-run the same suite with caching enabled and share the delta.

2) TPS: reported numbers are request-level steady-state TPS (requests completed per second) given the prompt/output token lengths I noted (not token/sec). We instrument both requests/sec and tokens/sec in the dashboard; dashboard link above includes both graphs.

3) Alerts / regression monitoring: example alert we use in pilots — fail if average ROUGE-L drops by >4% on the canary set OR if p95 latency increases >30% vs the baseline within a 1-hour window. Alerts are surfaced via Slack and email and also create a ticket in the CS console. We can customize thresholds.

4) Node type & autoscaling: these runs were on 1x A5000-equivalent GPU (16GB) for rw-7b and rw-13b profiles, and on 2x A100-equivalent nodes for rw-70b. For Dedicated/private deployments we expose autoscaling policies — default policy is target CPU/GPU utilization and scales nodes with warm-up rules; typical spin-up time for additional nodes is 60-120s depending on region and image warm caching. For strict p95 SLOs during large bursts we recommend a combination of scheduled buffer capacity + warm standby nodes (we can provision reserved pool for the pilot).

I've attached the prompt CSV in both the original and a sanitized format for your infra team (acme_eval_prompts.csv). Marissa and Vanessa — looping you in to propose pilot operations and a mutual action plan.

Proposed immediate actions:
- Marissa: set up a 2-week pilot with reserved test pool (suggest 2x A5000-equivalent nodes for baseline).
- Vanessa: share onboarding docs and a short checklist for infra to run the CSV locally if they prefer.
- Sarah: confirm pilot kickoff slot Thu 3/26 10:00 PT and share the internal Slack channel for alerts.

Alex
